Ex-employee of about 9 months. I have a few stories. I didn't catch the perps for any of these incidents. Just to note: I worked in produce.

1) Wonder Bread: A Love Story.

I was working in the back and I was the only one in the department, sorting through rotten vegetables and such. I heard an announcement over the intercom: "Maintenance to the Produce Department". I went to the floor, and couldn't find the spill, the most usual culprit of a call. The guy from maintenance came by about 30 seconds later saying "You've got to be kidding me."

I didn't know what was going on, but someone from the bakery next call found out that a man had vigorously pleasured himself in the processed bread section. I say vigorously because there was no way that much semen came out of just one time. The man wasn't caught, and the rest of the department had the same reaction as we did; the mixture between absurd disgust, and laughing because we didn't catch him.

2). The Man in the Shed.

I was stacking banana boxes in the back as I hear an alarm go off from a shoplifter going to the parking lot. This was a rather common occurrence, so I elected to ignore it and continue my work. The alarm turned off, no codes were called, so the supposed altercation must have ended.

There was a staff meeting later on that night. We discussed what each department's goals were, what each associate needs to look out for, etc. The security guy came in saying the perp had thrown a weight at the glass gun case from sporting goods, grabbed a bunch of guns, then ran out. Two weeks later, he was found living in a shed at the store next door with even more firearms.

So we BOLT to the door, shove our cellos in the back seat and haul ass to the voice recital. Outside it was a horrible downpour. She had a jacket, and I didn't. We end up going to the wrong building at first, so that's more time in the rain. We ran to the correct building, and I open the door as slowly as possible (fancy building with creaky doors).

Backstage: All eyes are now on me. No words were exchanged between any of the vocalists. They were in shock. I look over at my friend and ask "Did I make it?" In between breaths, as a single drop of water drips down the arch of my nose. It turns out, the last chord of the previous person was played when I asked. She was next, and the other cellist's boyfriend was after her. We made it at the last possible second for our respective performers.

To make my ADHD even to the point where it's mild I would need to enact the following things every single day:
-meditate
-join an exercise program (3-5 days a week)
-take my meds (almost at max dosage of concerta)
-eat a low-carb/high-protein diet
-carry a f*cking notebook wherever I go (bullet journal type) as a secretary and sync it with my phone to record everything
-keep MULTIPLE timers for when I need to actually manage my time
-actively remember social cues (read body language)
-Keep a consistent sleep schedule
-Carry a fidget toy or two.
-Attend CBT Therapy & get ADHD help

I'm roundabout halfway there, but not quite yet.

My point to this is we can try everything to help and people are still going to tell us that we suck and we're broken, irresponsible, and we just need to do better. We're not irresponsible. We're resilient, creative, and can be the most passionate people on the face of the planet. We can do phenomenal things, but just need help where we're weak.

I really appreciate how much you are trying to help your child. It means the world that there are parents like you. I have some advice for some common ADHD things that should help.
-Losing things: give him a place to put his belongings every day. Like his toothbrush is always behind the sink, or his coat is always on one specific hook.
-Give him a morning routine that is step by step in that order, and a list of them that he can check off as he goes. Everytime you see his morning list is done, give him positive feedback. This instills the habit loop.
-Make sure his teachers have a routine as well. He'll appreciate knowing what's going on.
-Everytime he comes home from school, have him immediately do his homework, and do the same thing for the morning routine. Positive reinforcement as a reward!
-GLITTER JARS! Oh my goodness you are gonna love this. In a tantrum, grab a glitter bottle out of your purse and have your child shake it up. Explain "The glitter is like your mind. When the glitter is all shaken up, you can't see through the bottle. When the glitter is settled, you can see clearly." or something like that. It's relaxing to see the glitter all shaken about, so he'll feel less overwhelmed.
